hero.headline: Anthropic settles copyright lawsuit for $1.5 billion
hero.body:
Anthropic's landmark $1.5B copyright settlement is approved

A federal court has approved a $1.5 billion settlement between AI company Anthropic and copyright holders, marking a significant legal resolution in the artificial intelligence industry. The settlement concludes a lawsuit over Anthropic's use of copyrighted material to train its AI models.

The approval represents an important financial and legal milestone for Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI assistant. The settlement amount reflects the substantial volume of copyrighted content incorporated into large language models and the escalating legal risks facing AI companies as they expand their training datasets.

While this settlement resolves the immediate case, it does not establish broader legal precedent for how copyright law applies to AI training practices. The fundamental question of whether using copyrighted works to train AI models constitutes fair use or copyright infringement remains legally unsettled. Other AI companies, including OpenAI and Meta, face similar legal challenges from authors, publishers, and artists who contend their work was used without permission or adequate compensation.

The settlement arrives as AI companies work to develop more capable systems while operating within an uncertain legal framework. Building advanced AI systems requires enormous quantities of text, images, and other data, much of which is protected by copyright. The companies have maintained that this use qualifies as transformative fair use under copyright law, while rights holders argue it represents unauthorized commercial exploitation of their creative work.

Training data remains one of the most contentious issues in AI development. Companies need vast datasets to build competitive models, but sourcing this data legally while respecting copyright protections presents a significant challenge. The tension between AI development and copyright protection has created a complex landscape where companies operate without clear legal guidelines.

The approval of this settlement may influence ongoing negotiations in other copyright disputes against AI companies. However, because this case was resolved through settlement rather than court judgment on the merits, it does not provide legal clarity on the fundamental copyright questions at stake. The legal framework governing AI training data remains fundamentally unsettled.

Industry observers expect that Congress and courts will continue addressing how existing copyright law applies to artificial intelligence technology. As more AI companies face similar litigation, the need for legal clarity becomes more urgent. Courts may eventually need to establish clearer guidelines about what constitutes acceptable use of copyrighted material in AI training.

The case highlights broader tensions in the AI industry between rapid technological development and respect for intellectual property rights. While Anthropic has now resolved this particular lawsuit, the underlying legal questions will likely shape how AI companies approach data sourcing and training practices for years to come. Until courts establish clearer precedent or Congress passes new legislation, AI companies will continue navigating an uncertain regulatory environment.

cards.headline: US conducts tenth night of strikes against Iran after casualties mount
cards.body:
The United States has launched its tenth consecutive round of airstrikes against Iranian targets as the military campaign intensifies following the deaths of three American service members and injuries to nearly 100 others in recent weeks.

President Trump has vowed retaliation for the deaths of American soldiers as US forces continue their aerial campaign. In response, Iran's Revolutionary Guards have struck American military installations and vessels in the region, including targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and Qatar. Iran claims to have hit two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, though the US military disputes these reports.

The escalating conflict centers on control of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and gas supply passed before the fighting resumed. The current round of violence follows the collapse of a memorandum of understanding signed by both countries in June that was intended to keep the strait open for shipping and allow room for negotiations.

Both countries have interpreted the shipping agreement differently, with Iran attacking vessels that followed US-designated transit routes. Shipping traffic in the waterway has dropped significantly as violence has intensified, though most ships that continue to transit use the Iranian route.

US strikes have targeted Iranian military infrastructure, including bridges in the Hormozgan province, a tower at Chabahar port, and electrical infrastructure. Iranian state media reported that at least 38 people were killed and more than 400 wounded by Friday morning. Iran's energy ministry has urged citizens to reduce electricity and air conditioning use after power plants sustained damage from US strikes.

The IRGC has threatened severe consequences for countries hosting US military bases if American attacks on civilian infrastructure continue. According to Iranian state media, the Revolutionary Guards targeted US combat aircraft at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain, an intelligence center in Bahrain, a naval fuel pier in Kuwait, and a communications center in Kuwait.

Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz while the United States has reimposed a blockade on Iranian ports and ships. The US military said it boarded one ship and redirected three others attempting to break the blockade since it began on Tuesday.

The conflict has had economic ripple effects across the region and globally. Average US diesel prices have climbed above five dollars per gallon, with gasoline reaching nearly four dollars. These prices represent significant increases from a year ago, reflecting the broader economic impact of the renewed hostilities.

Even as military operations continue, diplomats report that de-escalation talks are ongoing. However, with neither side showing signs of backing down, questions remain about when or how this cycle of escalating military exchanges might be reversed.

cards.headline: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian imports as trade tensions escalate
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods on Monday, claiming that Canada has unfairly discriminated against American automobiles, alcohol and dairy products. The White House said the new duties will apply to a broad range of items, including wine, hockey sticks and cement, and will even cover goods previously protected under the United States-Mexico-Canada trade agreement.

The tariffs exclude energy products, fish, critical minerals and potash. Products already subject to import taxes for national security reasons, such as steel and aluminum, are also exempt. The White House will implement the duties in 30 days, providing a window for potential negotiations between the two countries.

Trump justified the tariffs through three proclamations issued under Section 338 of the 1930 Trade Act. He argued that Canada maintained a 25% tariff on certain American motor vehicles and that several Canadian provinces blocked the sale of American alcoholic beverages while allowing imports from other nations. Trump also objected to what he described as Canadian discrimination against American cheese compared to European dairy products.

The White House official previewing the tariffs said Trump has also requested aides explore additional levies related to Canadian wildfires. Trump raised this issue Sunday while attending the World Cup final with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, saying Canada must stop fires from "poisoning our air."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by saying his government had submitted comprehensive proposals to resolve the trade dispute. He stated that Trump's previous tariffs violated their trade agreement and called for intensive negotiations to address the disagreement. Carney noted that the trade conflict has already increased costs for families on both sides of the border.

Political leaders across Canada expressed frustration with the action. Ontario Premier Doug Ford said that if the tariffs proceed, Canada should respond "tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar." Conservative opposition members called the tariffs an unjustified attack on Canadian workers and businesses.

Candace Laing, CEO of the Canadian chamber of commerce, described Trump's moves as regrettable but urged both countries to use the 30-day period before implementation to make meaningful progress in formal talks.

Economists warn the tariffs could trigger significant economic disruption. Higher import duties typically raise prices for American consumers on goods containing Canadian components. The two nations maintain deeply integrated supply chains, particularly in manufacturing, automotive and aerospace sectors. Analysts expect the tariffs to accelerate inflation concerns and potentially disrupt decades-old trading relationships developed under free trade agreements.

The new tariffs could carry serious political risks for Trump ahead of upcoming midterm elections, particularly if they cause market instability or consumer price increases similar to previous trade actions.

cards.headline: Three US service members killed in Iran conflict
cards.teaser: Weekend deaths leave White House allies concerned about the president's ability to exit the conflict.
cards.body:
Three U.S. service members were killed since Friday as tensions escalated between the U.S. and Iran. The deaths occurred amid a breakdown in peace negotiations between the two countries, which had centered on a memorandum of understanding regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

Following the casualties, both nations launched retaliatory strikes. The U.S. attacks marked the ninth consecutive day of bombing in the escalating conflict.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth requests $350 billion funding increase
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth will testify before Congress seeking a major defense budget boost as the Iran conflict continues.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will appear before Congress to request a $350 billion funding increase. The request comes as the war with Iran continues with no resolution in sight.

Hegseth's testimony before the Senate panel will address the escalating military needs in the Middle East. The substantial funding request reflects the ongoing costs of the conflict and the Defense Department's assessment of resources needed to sustain current operations.

cards.headline: Houthi rebels threaten blockade of Bab Al-Mandeb Strait
cards.teaser: Yemen's Houthi militia announced a naval blockade of the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait amid the US-Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

The Houthis, a Shiite militia in Yemen aligned with Iran, have announced a naval blockade of the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait, a critical waterway for international shipping connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

The blockade announcement reflects escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran. Fuel prices in the United States have risen sharply amid these geopolitical pressures, with diesel averaging over $5 a gallon and regular gas near $4—roughly $1.25 higher than a year prior.

cards.headline: Lebanese troops deploy in Israeli-held village under ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: The Israeli military withdrew from a Lebanese village as part of a US-brokered plan to return occupied areas to Lebanese control after months of conflict.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have withdrawn from a village in southern Lebanon as part of a US-brokered ceasefire agreement. The Lebanese army has moved into the area, which authorities are treating as a pilot zone to test the withdrawal process.

The agreement aims to return territory occupied by Israel during months of conflict with Hezbollah back to Lebanese government control. However, Hezbollah has rejected the truce despite the Israeli pullback from the small area.

cards.headline: Philippines reports sailor injured in clash with Chinese coast guard
cards.teaser: A Filipino sailor was wounded during a confrontation with Chinese coast guard forces in the latest South China Sea incident between the two countries.
cards.body:
The Philippines government said one of its sailors was injured during a skirmish with the Chinese coast guard in the South China Sea. China denied being the aggressor in the incident.

The clash marks the latest confrontation between Manila and Beijing over their overlapping territorial claims in the disputed waters. Both nations maintain military and coast guard operations in the resource-rich region, where tensions have repeatedly flared in recent years.

cards.headline: New UK prime minister orders cut to electricity taxes
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Andy Burnham moved quickly to address high living costs with a reduction in taxes on electricity.
cards.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a cut to VAT on household electricity bills on his first full day in office, aiming to ease the cost-of-living pressures facing British households. Homes will save approximately £45 annually through the reduction, which takes effect in October.

The move reflects Burnham's campaign pledge to provide financial relief to ordinary Britons struggling with economic pressures. The electricity tax cut represents one of his administration's early priorities as it takes office.

cards.headline: Flash floods kill at least 23 in Afghanistan
cards.teaser: Floods swept through a city in Nuristan province, leaving dozens missing in the isolated eastern region.
cards.body:
At least 23 people died after flash floods struck a city in Nuristan, a remote province in eastern Afghanistan. Dozens of people remained missing following the disaster, which overwhelmed the area with sudden rushing water.

Nuristan sits in an isolated part of the country where rugged terrain makes rescue and recovery operations difficult. The floods hit without warning, giving residents little time to seek safety. Afghan authorities have not yet released full casualty figures as search efforts continue in affected areas.

cards.headline: Protesters prompt response from Ukrainian President Zelensky
cards.teaser: With public anger high over the firing of the defense minister, the presidential office signals openness to compromise.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's office indicated a willingness to compromise following protests over the dismissal of the country's defense minister. The demonstrations reflected widespread anger among Ukrainians over the leadership change during the ongoing conflict.

The response follows a Ukrainian tradition of leaders engaging with public protests. Zelensky's office signaled it would listen to the concerns raised by demonstrators, though specific policy changes have not been announced. The protests represent a rare moment of domestic political tension in a country that has largely united behind its wartime leadership.

cards.headline: Venezuelan brothers search 26 days to recover family members killed in disaster
cards.teaser: Winder and Deivi Delfín dug daily to find the bodies of their mother, brother, and grandmother.
cards.body:
Two young brothers in Venezuela spent 26 days digging to recover the bodies of their mother, brother, and grandmother who died in an unspecified disaster. Winder and Deivi Delfín conducted the search themselves, working each day to locate their family members.

The recovery effort highlights the challenges faced by families seeking to retrieve loved ones in Venezuela. The brothers' determination to find and properly bury their relatives led them to continue the physically demanding work for nearly a month until they succeeded in their mission.

hero.headline: Men enter nursing in rising numbers, seeking stable careers
hero.body:
Men now represent about one in eight nurses in the United States, a share that continues to grow as strong job prospects and targeted recruitment efforts draw more men into the profession. The trend reflects both the robust demand for nursing professionals and sustained campaigns to diversify a field historically dominated by women.

The shift appears particularly pronounced in the South, where healthcare systems have actively worked to attract male candidates to nursing programs and clinical positions. Men pursuing nursing cite job security and stable career paths as primary motivations for entering the field.

The nursing profession has experienced sustained growth in recent years, driven by an aging population, expanded healthcare coverage, and increasing demand for medical services. Job market conditions for nurses remain strong across most regions, with healthcare facilities reporting persistent need for qualified staff.

Recruitment initiatives have focused on reshaping perceptions of nursing as a career suitable for all genders. These efforts have included outreach to high schools and community colleges, mentorship programs pairing male nursing students with established professionals, and marketing campaigns highlighting the clinical, technical, and leadership aspects of nursing work.

Despite the growth, men still represent a small minority of the nursing workforce. The increase in male nurses follows broader patterns in other traditionally gender-segregated occupations, where economic factors and changing social attitudes have gradually shifted workforce composition over time.

cards.headline: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump imposed 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, citing unfair discrimination against American products.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump imposed 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods on Monday, citing unfair discrimination against American products in the automotive, alcohol, and dairy sectors. The tariffs apply to a wide range of items including wine, hockey sticks, and cement, and cover goods previously protected under the United States-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) agreement.

The move follows Canada's retaliation against earlier US tariffs. Trump's administration characterized the action as a response to what it views as discriminatory Canadian trade policies that harm American producers and manufacturers across multiple industries.

cards.headline: US conducts additional strikes on Iran as conflict intensifies
cards.teaser: The United States launched fresh strikes on Iran as President Trump warned of retaliation for American soldier deaths.
cards.body:
The US military has launched its 10th consecutive round of strikes on Iran, with the goal of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump acknowledged three US military casualties and vowed retaliation, saying the fallen soldiers "were out there fighting that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon."

Iran's president declared the country is in a "full-scale war" following the expanded American aerial campaign. Iran reported striking two ships in the Strait of Hormuz and targeting locations in Bahrain and Jordan. Despite the escalating military actions, diplomats said de-escalation talks continue between the two nations.

cards.headline: Soccer connects Bhutanese refugee community in Harrisburg
cards.teaser: Harrisburg's large Nepali-speaking Bhutanese community uses soccer to maintain cultural ties and build connections across generations.
cards.body:
Harrisburg, Pennsylvania is home to one of the nation's largest communities of Nepali-speaking Bhutanese refugees and their families. Soccer has become a vital way for the community to build connection and belonging across generations.

Through the sport, families maintain their shared history while establishing roots in the United States. Soccer games and leagues serve as gathering spaces where cultural traditions are preserved and younger generations learn about their heritage.

cards.headline: Inquest opens into death of Ann Widdecombe
cards.teaser: A coroner's inquest heard that the cause of death for former politician Ann Widdecombe has not yet been determined.
cards.body:
An inquest into Ann Widdecombe's death heard that the cause has not yet been established. The 78-year-old was found with visible injuries at her home in Devon on July 9.

Widdecombe had a long career as a Conservative MP and went on to become a prominent media personality and political commentator.

cards.headline: UK borrows less than forecast in June
cards.teaser: The United Kingdom borrowed less money than expected last month, though the country continues to carry substantial debt.
cards.body:
Public finances in the United Kingdom performed better than anticipated in June, with the government borrowing less than economists had forecast. The figures offered a modest bright spot for the country's fiscal position.

Despite the better than expected monthly result, the UK continues to manage substantial debt levels. Public finances remain a challenge for policymakers as they balance spending commitments against the need to control borrowing over the longer term.

cards.headline: UK to cut electricity VAT in October, saving households 45 pounds yearly
cards.teaser: The British government announced it will reduce value-added tax on household electricity bills starting in October.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government announced the VAT cut on electricity bills on his first full day in office. The reduction will save households approximately 45 pounds per year.

The tax cut aims to reduce the cost of living for British families facing elevated energy prices. The policy represents one of the new government's first economic measures since Burnham took office.

cards.headline: Thames Water lenders propose golden share to prevent nationalization
cards.teaser: Creditors of the struggling water utility are offering the British government a golden share to avoid a government takeover.
cards.body:
Thames Water's lenders have proposed giving the government a golden share in the company as an alternative to full nationalization. The move comes as the water supplier faces mounting financial pressures that have prompted the government to consider taking over operations.

The lenders are preparing for the possibility of nationalization, with creditors ready to pursue full payment of outstanding debts worth billions of pounds if the takeover proceeds. The golden share proposal represents an attempt to preserve private ownership while addressing the company's stability concerns.

cards.headline: China injects record funds into tech ETF to support stock market
cards.teaser: Chinese authorities directed record investment into a technology exchange-traded fund as part of expanded efforts to stabilize markets.
cards.body:
State-owned funds purchased nearly 9 billion dollars in shares to support the Chinese stock market. The intervention included record inflows into a technology-focused ETF, broadening the government's market rescue efforts beyond previous targets.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission pledged to maintain market stability as A-shares rebounded following the coordinated buying. The government intervention reflects concern about sustained declines in Chinese equity markets and their technology sector.

cards.headline: General Motors raises 2026 outlook after beating earnings estimates
cards.teaser: GM reported better than expected quarterly earnings and increased its full-year guidance, citing premium pricing on trucks and cost reductions.
cards.body:
General Motors beat earnings expectations and raised its 2026 financial outlook. The automaker attributed the results to resilient pricing for premium trucks and successful cost-cutting measures.

GM announced increased shareholder payouts following the strong profit performance. The company's ability to maintain premium pricing despite slowing overall sales volumes supported the improved outlook.

cards.headline: Asian stocks advance as global markets recover from AI sector sell-off
cards.teaser: Stock markets in South Korea and Japan rebounded after recent declines in artificial intelligence and technology shares.
cards.body:
World equity markets gained as Asian stocks recovered some losses from AI-related sell-offs. South Korean and Japanese markets led the advance as concerns about Middle East tensions eased and oil prices moderated.

Emerging market assets rallied on news of diplomatic efforts in the region and China's technology sector support measures. The rebound suggested investors were reassessing risks after recent technology stock declines.

cards.headline: UK public borrowing in June comes in below forecasts
cards.teaser: British government borrowing last month was lower than economists expected, though the country continues to carry substantial debt.
cards.body:
UK public finances for June showed better than anticipated results, with borrowing below forecast levels. The figures provided some relief to officials managing the country's fiscal position.

Despite the improved monthly numbers, Britain continues to face challenges from its accumulated debt burden. The public finance data arrived as the new Burnham government prepares its first budget plans.

cards.headline: Construction robotics startup Gritt raises $34 million
cards.teaser: Gritt emerged from stealth mode with funding to automate construction site tasks starting with solar plants.
cards.body:
Gritt has exited stealth mode with $34 million in funding to develop robots for construction site automation. The company is targeting the most challenging manual tasks on construction sites, starting with solar plant installations.

As renewable energy projects scale across the country, Gritt's initial focus on solar construction addresses a timely market need. The startup plans to expand its robotic systems to tackle a wider range of construction applications in the future.

cards.headline: Trump administration AI standards director resigns
cards.teaser: The leadership position at the Center for AI Standards and Innovation has become a revolving door.
cards.body:
The director of the Center for AI Standards and Innovation has resigned, marking another departure from a role that has experienced frequent turnover since David Sacks stepped down as AI czar.

The revolving door leadership at the center, which was created to develop artificial intelligence guidelines for government and industry use, raises concerns about consistency in the Trump administration's AI policy direction.

cards.headline: De-extinction startup Colossal seeks up to $30 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Colossal Biosciences is in talks to raise capital at double or triple its previous valuation.
cards.body:
Colossal Biosciences is in talks to raise new capital at a valuation between $20 billion and $30 billion. This would represent a significant jump from the company's previous funding round, potentially doubling or tripling its earlier valuation.

The de-extinction startup uses genetic engineering to revive extinct species, including the woolly mammoth and the Tasmanian tiger.

cards.headline: Google Photos adds toggle between AI and classic search
cards.teaser: Users can now switch between traditional search and Ask Photos AI assistant with one tap.
cards.body:
Google Photos introduced a toggle allowing users to quickly switch between its classic search function and the Ask Photos AI feature. The update addresses user feedback about the different search experiences.

The toggle appears in the search interface on both Android and iOS versions of Google Photos. The feature gives users a quick fix when Ask Photos AI results do not meet their needs, allowing them to fall back to traditional keyword-based search.

cards.headline: Pennsylvania officer charged with photographing nude prisoners
cards.teaser: A police officer allegedly covered his body camera to take photos of prisoners on his iPhone.
cards.body:
A Pennsylvania police officer was charged with oppression and obstruction after allegedly photographing nude prisoners on his personal iPhone. The officer reportedly covered his body camera while taking the photos, but other surveillance cameras recorded his actions.

District attorneys brought charges based on evidence from the additional cameras that captured the officer's conduct. The case involves allegations that the officer violated the rights of individuals in custody by taking unauthorized photographs.

hero.headline: Spain's World Cup champions parade before nearly 2 million in Madrid
hero.body:
Spain's men's national soccer team returned home to a massive celebration in Madrid following their World Cup victory. Nearly 2 million people filled the streets of the Spanish capital to honor the champions during an open-top bus parade through the city on Monday.

The team captured the World Cup title after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final held in New Jersey on Sunday. The players and coaching staff touched down at Madrid's Barajas airport at 2:30 p.m. local time before making their way through the city. The parade route centered around the Plaza de Cibeles in central Madrid, where crowds lined the streets to catch a glimpse of the trophy and celebrate with the squad.

The turnout represented one of the largest public gatherings in recent Spanish history. Many supporters had stayed out late into the night on Monday to welcome the team home, with some still recovering from the excitement of watching the final. The victory festivities drew an estimated crowd of almost 2 million Spaniards who descended on central Madrid.

The team's success came after Luis de la Fuente employed a team-focused approach throughout the tournament. Spain's ability to build a cohesive unit proved successful in securing the championship. The squad had not conceded a goal throughout their World Cup campaign, demonstrating their defensive strength and collective organization.

The squad was afforded official recognition beyond the public celebration. The players and coaching staff met with Spain's royal family and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to mark the historic achievement. This reflected the national significance placed on the team's accomplishment for the country.

Following the final, Lionel Messi addressed Argentine supporters about their loss. The Argentine captain acknowledged the support from fans but noted that the disappointment would take time to process. For Argentina, the defeat marked a difficult conclusion to their World Cup campaign, despite entering the tournament with high expectations and strong performances in earlier rounds.

The final itself drew significant global attention. Donald Trump, the U.S. president, remained prominently positioned during the trophy ceremony in New Jersey, standing alongside FIFA President Gianni Infantino as Spain celebrated their victory. The moment marked the second consecutive major tournament in which Trump positioned himself centrally during another nation's championship celebration.

The World Cup victory represented a historic achievement for Spanish soccer and demonstrated the effectiveness of their possession-based approach and defensive organization that has defined the team for the past 15 to 20 years. The massive public response in Madrid reflected how deeply the achievement resonated with the Spanish population and cemented the team's place in the country's sporting history.

cards.headline: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott rejects new contract offer
cards.teaser: England Under-21 international turns down extension as Premier League clubs show interest in the midfielder.
cards.body:
Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract offer from the club. The England Under-21 international's rejection comes as several Premier League sides express interest in securing his services.

Scott's decision to decline the extension leaves his future at Bournemouth in doubt as the transfer window continues.

cards.headline: Scottie Scheffler headlines field at 3M Open debut
cards.teaser: The world's top-ranked golfer makes his first appearance at TPC Twin Cities this week.
cards.body:
Scottie Scheffler enters the 3M Open as the betting favorite following his recent near-miss at the Open Championship. The world number one golfer is making his debut at the Minnesota tournament, marking a rare visit by the sport's top-ranked player to the event at TPC Twin Cities.

Scheffler's participation represents a significant draw for the tournament, which typically does not attract the highest-ranked players on tour. His recent performance at the Open Championship, where he came close to victory, has positioned him as the clear favorite heading into the week's competition.

cards.headline: ESPN parts ways with NFL analyst Ryan Clark
cards.teaser: The network has ended its relationship with the former player turned broadcaster, with additional layoffs expected.
cards.body:
ESPN has ended its relationship with NFL analyst Ryan Clark as part of a broader round of layoffs at the sports network. Clark, who provided analysis for ESPN's NFL coverage, learned of the decision and still appeared on the network's programming the following day.

The staff reductions extend beyond ESPN to include NFL Network, which is also implementing cuts. Additional layoffs across both networks were expected in the days following the initial announcements.

cards.headline: Portland Trail Blazers reject city's proposed arena term sheet
cards.teaser: Team officials say the proposal for Moda Center payments is a non-starter as arena negotiations stall.
cards.body:
A top Trail Blazers official has dismissed Portland's draft term sheet for a new arena deal, stating the organization has no interest in the payment structure proposed by the city. The breakdown in negotiations raises questions about the team's long-term future in Portland despite both sides expressing a desire to reach an agreement.

The city's proposal included specific payment terms related to the Moda Center that the Blazers and team owner Todd Dundon find unacceptable. Portland City Council President indicated the team has shown no willingness to engage with the payment framework outlined in the term sheet. Some fans view the ongoing negotiations as an important step toward securing the team's presence in the city.

cards.headline: UK authorities seize counterfeit sports kits worth £18 million
cards.teaser: Police confiscated fake football shirts during the World Cup due to safety concerns about fire risk.
cards.body:
UK police seized counterfeit football shirts valued at over £18 million during the World Cup period. The operation targeted fake kits being sold to consumers across the country.

The Fire Service warned that the counterfeit clothing poses fire hazards to wearers. The fake shirts fail to meet proper safety regulations and manufacturing standards, making them potentially dangerous to consumers who unknowingly purchase the unauthorized merchandise.

cards.headline: England teenager Erica Meg Parkinson works with mindset coach
cards.teaser: The young player has enlisted help from a mental performance specialist who previously worked with elite rugby and cricket teams.
cards.body:
England's Erica Meg Parkinson has brought a mindset coach into her support team. The mental performance specialist has previously worked with the All Blacks rugby team and former England cricketer Ashley Giles.

The addition reflects how young athletes are increasingly prioritising mental preparation as part of their development. Parkinson's appointment of a coach with elite-level experience underscores her commitment to building a comprehensive approach to her international career.

hero.headline: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Opens With Record-Breaking Box Office in UK and Ireland
hero.body:
Universal Pictures' The Odyssey captured the top spot at the UK and Ireland box office with a debut weekend of 12.5 million pounds, equivalent to $16.8 million. The film's opening represents Christopher Nolan's second-biggest premiere in the market, surpassing the performance of Oppenheimer.

The strong debut was driven by significant attendance at premium format screenings, which contributed to the film's overall performance across theaters in both countries. The Odyssey displaced the previous weekend's top film as audiences turned out for Nolan's latest project.

Nolan's decision to adapt Homer's ancient epic surprised many in the industry. After the massive success of Oppenheimer, which earned close to a billion dollars worldwide and won seven Academy Awards, the filmmaker had the freedom to pursue any project. He chose to bring The Odyssey to the screen at an unprecedented scale and level of artistic ambition.

The film stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, King of Ithaca, alongside Anne Hathaway as Penelope and Tom Holland as Telemachus. The story follows the battle-worn hero's 10-year journey home after the Trojan War, filled with encounters with monsters, gods, spirits, and sirens.

According to Nolan, The Odyssey's narrative structure has influenced cinema far more than people realize. "Whether it's the narrative through-line of Odysseus or the singular episodes that make up the epic, The Odyssey underpins almost all of cinema," Nolan explained. "It's certainly there in every movie I've ever done, to a degree I never before realised."

Nolan's wife and producing partner Emma Thomas revealed that the idea came from their family. "All our kids are into classical mythology, but one of them, Oliver, really loves these stories," she said. "Oliver said: 'What about The Odyssey? Nobody's really done that in a big movie form.' As soon as he said it, Chris and I both looked at each other, clearly thinking the same thing: He's absolutely right."

The Odyssey has already generated significant critical praise. Reviewers have described it as "a colossal piece of cinema," with the film drawing audiences to theaters for its visual spectacle and storytelling.

The UK and Ireland market represents a significant territory for Hollywood releases, often serving as an indicator of broader international appeal. Premium format screenings, including IMAX and other large-screen experiences, have become increasingly important revenue drivers for event films. The Odyssey's strong performance in these formats demonstrates continued audience appetite for large-scale theatrical experiences, particularly when paired with filmmakers known for delivering ambitious spectacle and narratives that reward the cinema experience.

cards.headline: Chloe Fineman Leaves Saturday Night Live After Seven Seasons
cards.teaser: The comedian departed the sketch show and recounted calling producer Lorne Michaels during a World Cup match to share the news.
cards.body:
Chloe Fineman has departed Saturday Night Live after seven seasons. She announced the news at the premiere of Apple TV's The Dink in Los Angeles, describing the decision as bittersweet.

When Fineman called producer Lorne Michaels to inform him of her exit, he was watching the England versus Argentina World Cup match. He told her he would call back once the game finished. Fineman revealed she has been crying over leaving the show.

cards.headline: Ryan Reynolds Confirms Future Deadpool Movie in Development
cards.teaser: The actor said another film featuring the Marvel character will eventually happen, focusing on lesser-known elements from the comics.
cards.body:
Ryan Reynolds confirmed at Fanatics Fest that another Deadpool movie is coming, though he noted it will happen "eventually." The actor revealed the film will draw from lesser-known material in the character's comic book history that hasn't yet made it to the screen.

Reynolds called these planned storylines "deep cuts" from the Deadpool comics. The Marvel antihero, known for fourth-wall breaks and R-rated humor, has appeared in multiple films with Reynolds in the lead role.

cards.headline: A.R. Rahman Launches Immersive App for Apple Vision Pro
cards.teaser: The Oscar-winning composer is releasing an app showcasing a decade of work in immersive storytelling formats.
cards.body:
A.R. Rahman is releasing ARR Immersive, an app for Apple Vision Pro that launches on July 22. The application features work from the composer's decade-long exploration of immersive storytelling, including projects in virtual reality and 360-degree formats.

Rahman won two Academy Awards for his work on Slumdog Millionaire and also composed music for 127 Hours. The app draws from his earlier project Le Musk, a 360-degree virtual reality film that premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. The release marks an expansion of Rahman's creative work into spatial computing platforms.

cards.headline: FAST Provider Wedotv Launches Four Channels in India on Samsung TV Plus
cards.teaser: The streaming service struck its first distribution agreement in the country, reaching Samsung Smart TV users.
cards.body:
Wedotv has expanded into India through a new distribution partnership with Samsung TV Plus. The FAST provider is now offering four channels to Samsung Smart TV users across the country: wedotv Big Stories, wedotv Cars, wedotv Movies, and wedotv Sports.

This marks wedotv's first distribution deal in India. The Big Stories channel is produced in collaboration with Big Pictures, while the other channels focus on automotive content, films, and sports. The launch gives the streaming service access to millions of Samsung television owners in the Indian market.

cards.headline: Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap Serves as Jury President at Malaysia International Film Festival
cards.teaser: The Indian director is leading the jury and conducting a masterclass while his latest film marks his return to directing.
cards.body:
Anurag Kashyap is serving as jury president at the Malaysia International Film Festival while also leading a masterclass titled Unfiltered Realism. The Indian filmmaker's latest directorial feature, Bandar, represents his return to directing after a period away from the camera.

Kashyap told the festival he hopes to discover something new in his role as jury president rather than claiming to have all the answers. The veteran filmmaker has built a reputation for realistic storytelling throughout his career. His presence at MIFFest includes both evaluating competition entries and sharing his filmmaking approach with attendees.

cards.headline: Abbey Road Studio to Honor Photographer Masayoshi Sukita With Lifetime Achievement Award
cards.teaser: The recording studio's annual photography awards will recognize the Japanese photographer at a ceremony in London.
cards.body:
The Abbey Road Music Photography Awards will present its Lifetime Achievement Award to Masayoshi Sukita at a ceremony in London this September. The recognition comes from the recording studio's annual photography awards program, which was established in 2022.

Sukita is known for his work photographing musicians and cultural figures throughout his career. The Abbey Road Music Photography Awards recognize excellence in music photography across multiple categories. The ceremony will take place at the studio's London location, continuing the tradition of honoring significant contributions to the field of music photography.

hero.headline: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
hero.body:
President Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods Monday, stating that Canada has unfairly discriminated against American automobiles, alcohol and dairy products. The move represents a significant escalation in trade tensions between the two nations.

The tariffs will affect a broad range of products, including wine, hockey sticks and cement. Notably, some goods previously protected under the United States-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) trade agreement will now face import taxes. However, the White House excluded energy products, fish, critical minerals and potash, as well as items already subject to tariffs related to national security concerns like steel and aluminum.

Trump justified the tariffs by pointing to Canadian retaliatory measures against earlier U.S. tariffs. According to White House statements, Canada maintains a 25% tariff on U.S. motor vehicles that don't qualify for USMCA protections. Additionally, most Canadian provinces and territories have stopped selling U.S. alcoholic beverages while permitting imports from other countries. Trump also objected to what he characterized as discriminatory treatment of American cheese compared to European dairy products.

The tariffs will take effect in 30 days, providing a window for potential negotiations between the countries. Trump signed three proclamations under Section 338 of the 1930 Trade Act to implement the increases.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by stating that his government has made comprehensive proposals to resolve trade disputes with Washington. "This trade dispute has raised costs for families, particularly in the US," Carney said. "Canada stands ready to engage intensively to address outstanding issues with the US to the mutual benefit of our citizens."

Ontario Premier Doug Ford called for Canada to respond "tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar" if the measures proceed. Candace Laing, CEO of the Canadian Chamber of Commerce, described the Trump administration's actions as "regrettable" but urged both countries to use the 30-day period to make meaningful progress in formal talks.

During a World Cup final attendance Sunday, Trump raised concerns about Canadian wildfire smoke affecting U.S. air quality with Carney. Trump stated on social media that Canada needed to stop fires from "poisoning our air." A White House official indicated that Trump has requested aides explore additional tariffs specifically related to wildfire smoke impacts on U.S. air quality.

The tariffs carry significant risks for Trump ahead of midterm elections. Previous "liberation day" tariffs in April triggered financial market concerns about inflation and recession, prompting the administration to negotiate reduced rates. The Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump had illegally used emergency executive power for global tariffs, forcing the administration to pursue alternative legal authorities.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth requests $350 billion funding increase
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth will testify before Congress seeking a major defense budget boost as the Iran conflict continues.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will appear before Congress to request a $350 billion funding increase. The request comes as the war with Iran continues with no resolution in sight.

Hegseth's testimony before the Senate panel will address the escalating military needs in the Middle East. The substantial funding request reflects the ongoing costs of the conflict and the Defense Department's assessment of resources needed to sustain current operations.

cards.headline: Three US service members killed in Iran conflict
cards.teaser: Weekend deaths leave White House allies concerned about the president's ability to exit the conflict.
cards.body:
Three U.S. service members were killed since Friday as tensions escalated between the U.S. and Iran. The deaths occurred amid a breakdown in peace negotiations between the two countries, which had centered on a memorandum of understanding regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

Following the casualties, both nations launched retaliatory strikes. The U.S. attacks marked the ninth consecutive day of bombing in the escalating conflict.

cards.headline: Republicans press Trump to reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers express alarm over rising oil prices as Iran ceasefire collapses.
cards.body:
Republican lawmakers are urging President Trump to find a way to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as oil prices surge following the collapse of a ceasefire with Iran. The closure of the strategic waterway has sparked concerns about voter backlash over rising gas prices.

The intensifying military conflict has reignited GOP alarm over economic consequences heading into the midterm elections. Oil prices have climbed again since the ceasefire fell apart, creating political pressure on the administration to resolve the crisis quickly.

cards.headline: House GOP leaders rush to pass stopgap funding bill
cards.teaser: Republican leadership seeks to avoid a government shutdown ahead of the October 1 deadline.
cards.body:
House GOP leaders are working to pass a stopgap funding measure that would fund the government from October 1 through December 4. The measure would give lawmakers additional time to complete the annual appropriations process.

The effort represents a shift in strategy for House Republicans, who are attempting to avoid the government shutdowns that have caused political damage in the past. The short-term extension would prevent a funding lapse while negotiations on full-year spending bills continue.

cards.headline: Trump to meet Lebanese President Aoun at White House
cards.teaser: Meeting comes as Lebanese leader seeks to reduce Hezbollah's influence while managing tensions with Israel.
cards.body:
President Trump is scheduled to meet with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House. The meeting will focus on the crisis in Lebanon as Aoun works to drain support from Hezbollah.

The meeting represents a critical moment for Aoun as he navigates competing pressures in Lebanon. The Lebanese president is attempting to demonstrate he can stand up to Israel while also reducing the influence of Hezbollah within his country.

cards.headline: Cyclospora cases rise amid federal health agency cuts
cards.teaser: Experts say staffing and funding reductions have hampered the government's disease response.
cards.body:
Cases of cyclospora are increasing as the Trump administration's cuts to staffing and funding at federal health agencies hamper response efforts. State and local health departments are also facing chronic underfunding.

Experts and former federal officials describe a complicated mix of issues that have converged to slow the government's reaction to the outbreak. The combination of reduced federal capacity and inadequate state resources has created challenges in tracking and responding to the parasitic infection.
